p0.title: M504 all-write cycles are paired with M473 no-forward read traffic, overstating the component-energy reduction
evidence: The analyzer uses aggregate_cycles.m504_all_write_1rw_cycles but reads parent_scratch_read_bytes from traffic.rows[design=m473_fused_concurrent_1r1w_ceiling] at source lines 166 and 175-179.
The selected M473 row charges 20,972,608,128 read bytes = 18,205,389 parent edges x 8 output banks x 144 B.

The frozen M505 result records the actual M504 single-port all-write schedule as 16,490,761 macro reads, 1,714,628 same-address RAW forwards, and 27,305,568 macro writes per output block. Therefore the matching M504 read traffic is 18,997,356,672 B, not 20,972,608,128 B.

The dead-write-only schedule also performs 16,490,761 macro reads and 9,947,701 macro writes per output block, so the all-write-versus-dead-write ablation changes writes and runtime, not the RAW-forwarded read count.
Using the source's slow-corner constants, the current wrong pairing yields baseline/candidate 3.4316117399458976/2.0396326002588162 mJ per frame and 40.56342165646709 percent reduction.
The semantically paired M504 traffic yields baseline/candidate 3.3018888289181215/2.0396326002588162 mJ per frame, 1.2622562286593053 mJ saved, and 38.228307918921945 percent reduction.
p0.impact: The proposed exact component-energy number is high by 2.335113737545145 percentage points and the saved-energy number is high by 0.1297229110277762 mJ/frame. A formal result would be numerically false even though the unit conversion is correct.
p0.required_repair: Expose a unique M504 all-write traffic row from a newly sealed M528 result, or add and freeze the sealed M505 result and derive M504 reads/writes from its admitted aggregate. Enforce M504 reads + forwards = parent edges, M504 writes = active rows, and dead-only read equality before recomputing the expected component reduction.

p1.title: Three frozen input digests are caller-selected rather than analyzer-bound
evidence: Only docs/359 has a hard-coded expected digest.
--m528-result-sha256, --m528-hammer-sha256, and --macro-map-sha256 are arbitrary required CLI strings, then source lines 122-131 compare each file only with the caller-provided string.
The analyzer neither loads the M593 source contract nor compares those three CLI digests with the contract's frozen values 778c8e1b..., 4f70610d..., and 68017fb5....
A modified input plus its newly computed digest therefore passes the analyzer's SHA loop; there is not yet a sealed exact runner that narrows this surface.
p1.impact: The source alone does not implement the requested strict frozen-input identity and could price a substituted ledger while emitting the same result schema.
p1.required_repair: Hard-code all frozen digests, or require and verify the exact source-contract path/SHA and compare every CLI path/digest with its frozen entry before parsing. A later runner may add defense in depth but must not be the only binding.

p2.title: Future output rows do not retain traffic provenance or the RAW-forward conservation split
p2.evidence: The future row is renamed all_write_1rw_parent_scratch but carries no traffic_source, read/forward split, output-bank multiplier, or exact conservation predicate. This omission helped conceal the M473/M504 pairing error.
p2.required_repair: Emit source design/result identity, per-output-block reads/forwards/writes, bank count, word bytes, and the executed conservation checks in the bounded component result.

diagnostic_m505_result.use: independent semantic cross-check of M504 macro reads, forwards, writes, and cycles; not a production input to the reviewed analyzer

decision.only_allowed_next_step: author a new immutable M593 energy analyzer/source-contract identity with corrected M504 traffic semantics and analyzer-bound frozen digests, then request a fresh independent static hammer
